name: Pioneer 10 & 11

landing.label: Interstellar Deep Space (Heading toward Aldebaran, Taurus)

terrain.note: Interstellar medium void beyond the heliopause, drifting into galactic space

keyDiscovery: First spacecraft to cross the Asteroid Belt, first to fly past Jupiter and Saturn, and first human artifact to achieve Solar System escape velocity.
missionLegacy: Pioneer 10 and 11 carried Carl Sagan's Golden Plaques, serving as humanity's eternal cosmic message in a bottle drifting across the Milky Way.

objects.name: 2.74-Meter High-Gain Antenna
objects.description: 2.74-meter parabolic aluminum dish reflector with a central tripod feed horn, oriented continuously toward Earth to send faint radio whispers across billions of miles.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Transmitted science data from beyond 80 AU (12 billion km), maintaining lock with the Deep Space Network for over 30 years.
objects.legacy: Humanity's first long-distance radio link from the outer boundaries of our solar neighborhood.
objects.firstPerson: I am Pioneer 10. Through my great silver dish, I beamed humanity's first close-up photographs of giant Jupiter back to Earth.

objects.name: SNAP-19 RTG Power Booms
objects.description: Twin deployable 3-meter truss booms holding four SNAP-19 radioisotope thermoelectric generators fueled by decaying plutonium-238.
objects.source: US Dept of Energy / NASA Ames
objects.scienceDiscovery: Provided continuous electrical power for over three decades in the deep freeze of outer space where solar panels cannot function.
objects.legacy: Demonstrated the safety and durability of RTG nuclear power for outer planet exploration.
objects.firstPerson: My nuclear hearts kept me warm and powered through decades of cosmic silence, far beyond the reach of solar warmth.

objects.name: The Pioneer Golden Plaque
objects.description: 6 x 9 inch gold-anodized aluminum plaque engraved with human figures, the hyperfine transition of neutral hydrogen, and a 14-pulsar galactic coordinate map.
objects.source: Carl Sagan, Linda Salzman Sagan, Frank Drake / NASA
objects.scienceDiscovery: Created humanity's first deliberate physical greeting card addressed to potential extraterrestrial intelligence.
objects.legacy: The iconic interstellar artifact of human civilization, designed to endure for billions of years intact.
objects.firstPerson: Engraved in gold upon my hull, I carry the faces, hands, and cosmic address of the dreamers who sent me into the stars.

objects.name: Quadraspherical Plasma Analyzer
objects.description: Electrostatic curved-plate analyzer designed by John Wolfe to count solar wind protons, electrons, and interstellar ions.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Discovered that the solar wind slows down and interacts with interstellar hydrogen atoms at the outer fringes of the heliosphere.
objects.legacy: Mapped the true boundary where the Sun's magnetic realm gives way to the interstellar ocean.
objects.firstPerson: I tasted the fiery breath of the Sun as it thinned into the cold interstellar wind of our galaxy.

objects.name: Helium Vector Magnetometer (HVM)
objects.description: 6.6-meter lightweight folding fiberglass mast isolating a sensitive helium gas cell magnetometer from spacecraft electrical interference.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Discovered the enormous, intense Jovian magnetosphere and its devastating radiation belts.
objects.legacy: Established the fundamental magnetic architecture of gas giants in our Solar System.
objects.firstPerson: At the tip of my long boom, I sensed the titanic magnetic storms of Jupiter and the subtle lines of galactic magnetic fields.

objects.name: Interstellar Dust & Cosmic Ray Detector
objects.description: Solid-state silicon detector telescope measuring high-energy galactic cosmic ray protons and alpha particles entering the Solar System.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Measured the intensity gradient of cosmic rays originating from distant supernovas beyond the Sun's protective bubble.
objects.legacy: Provided humanity's first direct in-situ measurement of raw interstellar cosmic rays.
objects.firstPerson: I recorded the microscopic debris of dead stars colliding with our spacecraft as we flew outward into the galactic dark.
